title: Total cholesterol

review.note: Drafted from the source below; not yet reviewed by a medical professional.

measures: Total cholesterol is a measure of the total amount of cholesterol in the blood, including HDL and LDL cholesterol. Cholesterol is a waxy, fat-like substance the body needs to make hormones, vitamin D, and substances that help digest food.
context: You may need to fast for 9 to 12 hours before the blood draw, so the test is often done in the morning. A healthy level for a person can depend on age, family history, lifestyle, and other factors, and one result alone does not tell the whole story.
aboveRange: Eating foods high in dietary fat, which can raise the cholesterol in the blood
Excess weight and a lack of physical activity
Smoking and drinking too much alcohol, which can raise total cholesterol
Family history and genes, which cannot be changed
A higher total cholesterol can be associated with a greater risk of heart problems over time
nextStep: Discuss this result with your doctor.
